author: reek
body: An input draws a caret one pixel wide at its content origin plus six pixels per character of cursor index. Nothing holds that index inside the widget, so a cursor far enough along the text paints the caret outside the box it belongs to, over whatever sits to the right. This is the same shape as the gauge fill `gpu-gauge-clamp` pins, in the same chapter, one function away.

author: reek
body: It is reachable from a shipping program rather than hypothetical. `apps/cvmm` renders through `bare-app-render`, which is `gr-render-tree`, which dispatches `WkInput` here; and every filter box in that application sets its cursor to the LENGTH of the filter text, so the index grows with each character typed.

author: reek
body: The instrument has to scan outside the widget, because a caret one pixel wide is submitted and counted exactly as a correct one is, and a reading that asks only whether the caret is present answers yes in both worlds.

author: reek
body: The input carries no text, deliberately. The caret and the text are drawn in the same colour, so an outside hit against a non-empty input could be either; with the text empty, `pal-fg` outside the box can only be the caret. The sibling label is empty for the reason `gpu-gauge-clamp` gives: a label emits text and no box, so it paints nothing at all.

author: reek
body: Three readings, because no two of them can agree by accident. `box` is the control: the input's own border, which says the widget painted, and without which a renderer that drew nothing would report a clean outside and pass. `inside` and `outside` are where the caret landed.

author: reek
body: Sixty characters at six pixels each is 360, which is past the right edge of a widget pinned to 200.
